chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one in Ihram neither marries (himself) nor is married off, nor proposes marriage, nor witnesses a marriage; and if he marries, his marriage is invalid.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُنْكِحُ: He is married off (by a guardian)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage for a person in the state of Ihram during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that the state of Ihram imposes a comprehensive suspension of matrimonial capacity, rendering both the act of contracting marriage and serving as a witness legally void (batil). In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the spiritual purity required during Hajj, where the pilgrim is detached from worldly ties to focus solely on divine worship. The invalidity applies regardless of whether the Muhrim is the groom, bride, or witness, highlighting the ritual's restrictive nature on social contracts.
